rv.q: This musical, based on the 1983. Hollywood film, is not only derivative but also manipulative, hackneyed, sexist, noisy – and shameless good fun.
For all its internal contradictions, the piece is extremely well staged.
I left this supposedly feelgood show actually feeling both cheated and depressed.
The show’s fresh as masonry paint, a full-on power blast, striking sparks, and industrial action, in all directions.

The question is, will this new musical live up to the film? Despite having the original screenwriter Tom Hedley on board and the considerable choreographing talents of Arlene Phillips, the short answer is no.

cn.t: Critics find this 1980s movie adaptation loud, derivative, and cynically commercial, though the energetic choreography and dance sequences earn praise. Reception ranges from dismissive to moderately enthusiastic.
